app.title: Furniture Hooves
app.subtitle: Furniture riser boot generator
shape.label: Cross-section
hint.pos.bottom: Vertical hole in the floor centre – the screw goes up into the leg.
hint.pos.side: Horizontal hole through the left wall – the screw goes sideways into the leg.
help.legWidth: Leg size along X, measured with calipers where the boot will sit.
help.legDiameter: Diameter of a round leg, measured with calipers where the boot will sit.
help.legDepth: Leg size along Y. Locked to the width for squares.
help.legCornerRadius: Radius of the leg's vertical edges. 0 = sharp corners.
help.tolerance: Extra clearance added to the leg size – total, i.e. half on each side. Inner size = leg + tolerance.
help.lift: Floor thickness – how much the furniture is raised. Robot vacuums usually need 8–12 mm extra.
help.wallThickness: Thickness of the vertical sleeve wall around the leg.
help.sleeveHeight: How far the boot wraps the leg, measured from the bottom of the leg.
help.outerCornerRadius: Radius of the outer vertical edges. Must not thin the corner wall below 0.8 mm.
help.bottomChamfer: Chamfer of the outer bottom edge – compensates the first-layer “elephant foot”.
help.topChamfer: Inner chamfer at the top of the sleeve, makes sliding onto the leg easier.
help.screwEnabled: Hole for a small wood screw that keeps the boot on the leg when moving furniture – from below or from the side.
help.screwHoleDiameter: Hole diameter = screw diameter (e.g. 3 mm). The screw bites into the leg.
help.screwHead: Countersunk wood screw heads have a 90° cone – the hole gets the same chamfer so the head sits flush.
help.screwHeadDiameter: Countersunk head diameter (usually 6 mm for a 3 mm screw). The 90° cone depth = ¼ of the head diameter – only this drives the recess and the collar.
help.screwSideHeight: Height of the side hole axis above the cavity floor (above the leg bottom).
hint.tolerance: New furniture 0.5–1 mm · older, worn 1.5–3 mm
hint.wallThickness: Recommended: multiples of the 0.4 mm extrusion width (2.4 · 2.8 · 3.2)
err.cornerWall: The corner wall would be only {wall} mm (min. {min} mm).
err.belowLift: Must be smaller than the lift ({max} mm).
err.belowWall: Must be smaller than the wall thickness ({max} mm).
err.belowSleeve: Must be smaller than the sleeve height ({max} mm).
err.headVsHole: Head must be larger than the screw ({min} mm).
err.screwFit: Does not fit the inner area – max. {max} mm.
err.recessDepth: Recess of {depth} mm is too deep – max. {max} mm (floor ≥ 1 mm).
err.sleeveTooLow: The sleeve is too low for a side screw – increase the sleeve height.
warn.thinWall: Wall thinner than {min} mm – may be fragile.
warn.largeLift: High floor (over {max} mm) – consider reinforcement pillars and a wider base in Load & printing.
warn.zeroTolerance: Without tolerance the boot may not fit.
warn.sideBoss: The wall is too thin for the countersunk head – a +{extra} mm collar is added around the hole ({required} mm of material), chamfered 45° underneath → no supports.
viewer.title: 3D preview
viewer.error: The model could not be generated
viewer.invalid: Fix the invalid values – showing the last valid model.
viewer.invalidNoModel: Fix the invalid values in the panel – the model appears once they are valid.
viewer.tip: Print bottom down, no supports. 20–40 % infill; PETG and 4+ perimeters for heavy furniture.
viewer.webgl: Your browser does not support WebGL – no 3D preview, export still works.
export.notReady: The model is not ready yet.
export.invalid: Cannot export – fix the invalid values.
measure.title: How to measure a furniture leg
measure.intro: Accurate dimensions matter – the boot should sit tight but still slide on.
measure.s1: Measure the leg 1–2 cm above the floor, where the boot will wrap it. A ruler is imprecise, calipers are ideal.
measure.s2: For square legs measure width and depth separately – legs are rarely perfectly square. For round legs measure the diameter in two directions and use the larger value.
measure.s3: If the leg has rounded edges, estimate the radius (e.g. with a coin). Radii below 1 mm can be ignored.
measure.s4: New furniture with exact dimensions: 0.5–1 mm. Older, worn or lacquered: 1.5–3 mm. When in doubt, print a test piece with a low sleeve (e.g. 5 mm) first.
measure.s5: Measure the height of your robot vacuum and the gap under the furniture. Lift = vacuum height − gap + 3–5 mm reserve.
footer.note: Static app – everything is computed in your browser.
profile.label: Leg profile
help.legWidthBottom: Measure a tapered leg at its bottom (at the floor). It widens upwards by the given angle.
help.legDiameterBottom: Measure a conical leg at its bottom (at the floor). It widens upwards by the given angle.
help.legDepthBottom: Measure a tapered leg depth at its bottom (at the floor).
help.legTaperCone: Angle of the conical leg surface from vertical (per side). Typically 2–5°.
help.legTaperPyramid: Angle of the truncated-pyramid leg sides from vertical (per side). Typically 2–5°.
hint.legTaper: Measure the width at the bottom and 10 cm higher: angle ≈ atan((top − bottom) / 2 / 100)
help.topOuterChamfer: Chamfer of the outer edge at the top of the sleeve (45°) – nicer look, nothing catches on it.
err.topRim: Together with the lead-in less than {min} mm would remain on the top rim – max. {max} mm.
load.intro: Tell us what the furniture carries – the app recommends print settings and boot reinforcement.
help.weightKg: Estimated total weight: furniture plus whatever is in/on it (books, clothes, a mattress with people…).
help.legs: How many legs share the weight.
help.furnitureHeight: Overall furniture height – tall furniture is less stable once raised.
load.safetyNote: Pressures include a ×2 safety factor (uneven floor, moving furniture).
load.in3mf: The downloaded 3MF contains these settings – PrusaSlicer applies them automatically.
load.warn.tall: Tall furniture ({height} mm): raising it moves the centre of gravity up – anchor it to the wall (anti-tip).
load.warn.tallHighLift: Tall furniture ({height} mm) and a high lift ({lift} mm): less stable – definitely anchor it to the wall and widen the boot base.
load.warn.slender: A {lift} mm floor is high for the boot width – a wider base improves stability.
load.warn.extreme: Leg pressure of {mpa} MPa is very high – use reinforcement pillars, PETG and consider a larger contact area.
load.warn.softFloor: Higher floor pressure – on carpet, vinyl or cork a wider base helps.
help.reinforce: Hidden Ø 1 mm vertical voids in the floor – the slicer prints perimeters around them, forming solid columns. The boot carries heavy loads even with normal infill.
help.baseFlare: The bottom grows by this much on each side and returns to the wall at 45° (no supports). Better stability and lower floor pressure.
hint.baseFlare: For a high floor, tall furniture or soft floors.
err.flareLift: The flare must end below the cavity floor – max. {max} mm (or raise the floor).
warn.pillarsLift: Pillars need a floor of at least {min} mm.
viewer.tipDynamic: Print bottom down, no supports. Recommended: {infill} % infill, {perimeters} perimeters, {material}.
